# What is the temporary workaround validated by the original author for the service call triggering 500 Hz overrun in this case, and what root causes remain unknown?

> **Current answer:** In the Jazzy/4.38.0/UR environment, the author confirmed that switching RMW_IMPLEMENTATION from rmw_zenoh_cpp to rmw_fastrtps_cpp eliminated the phenomenon; it was reproducible on Zenoh 0.2.8 deb and 0.2.9 commit 858f7b5. Switching RMW can be used as an isolation method, but the cause of delay in the service/publish path in Zenoh is not identified, and Cyclone DDS is not provided in the post.

## Key terms

- Robot Operating System (ROS) middleware implementation (RMW) (机器人操作系统中间件实现)
- Control-loop overrun (控制环超时)
- Real-Time Data Exchange (RTDE) (实时数据交换)
- Service call (服务调用)

## Problem and symptoms

- How can one narrow down the issue to the RMW layer when calling the controller_manager service during a 500 Hz control loop overrun and UR RTDE disconnection?
- List_controllers is called once per second, causing an update delay of approximately 3.16 ms and a total cycle of approximately 3.33 ms, missing the 500 Hz deadline.
- Frequent calls lead to UR RTDE Data Pipeline overflow and disconnection.

## Environment

- Ubuntu 24.04; kernel 6.8.1-1037-realtime PREEMPT_RT; ROS 2 Jazzy; ros-jazzy-controller-manager 4.38.0-1noble.20251008.000820; rmw_zenoh 0.2.8 deb and 0.2.9 commit 858f7b5; Intel i7-11700.

## Priority diagnostics

- Fixing the ros2_control/controller_manager version, switching only RMW_IMPLEMENTATION for A/B.
- Comparing controller_manager.total_time before, during, and after the service call; the maintainer did not reproduce it on the same version locally, indicating it is not solely a controller_manager version issue.

## Possible causes

- The author confirmed the phenomenon occurs with rmw_zenoh, disappears when switching to Fast DDS; the internal lock and mechanism in Zenoh are not further identified.

## Attempts

- The author provided evidence of service calls, rqt, and system load; the maintainer measured the mutex region to be approximately 20 us.
- The author switched from rmw_zenoh to rmw_fastrtps and reproduced the issue on two Zenoh versions.

## Effective fixes

- Temporarily switching from rmw_zenoh to Fast DDS in this environment; the author also plans to use Cyclone DDS.

## Result

- The author confirmed that switching RMW alone eliminates the phenomenon; the root cause is not fully identified, and the issue was closed due to stale closure.

## Limitations

- Cannot conclude that all rmw_zenoh versions or all service calls have this issue.
- Cyclone DDS does not provide actual test data on this thread; it is only a plan by the author.
- The stale issue closure does not equal the root cause of Zenoh.

## Safety notes

- RMW switching should be validated on an experimental platform before restoring to real machine high-speed operation.
